  87def _xy(point: PointType) -> tuple[float, float]:
  88    x, y = point[:2]
  89    return (float(x) + 0.0, float(y) + 0.0)
  90
  91
  92def _triangle_vertices(
  93    triangle: TriangleLike,
  94) -> tuple[PointType, PointType, PointType]:
  95    if isinstance(triangle, Triangle):
  96        vertices = triangle.vertices
  97    else:
  98        vertices = tuple(triangle)
  99    if len(vertices) != 3:
 100        raise ValueError("A triangle must have three vertices.")
 101    return _xy(vertices[0]), _xy(vertices[1]), _xy(vertices[2])
 102
 103
 104def _side_lengths(
 105    p1: PointType, p2: PointType, p3: PointType
 106) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
 107    side_a = distance(p2, p3)
 108    side_b = distance(p3, p1)
 109    side_c = distance(p1, p2)
 110    return side_a, side_b, side_c
 111
 112
 113def _triangle_edges(
 114    p1: PointType, p2: PointType, p3: PointType
 115) -> tuple[tuple[PointType, PointType], ...]:
 116    p1, p2, p3 = _xy(p1), _xy(p2), _xy(p3)
 117    return ((p1, p2), (p2, p3), (p3, p1))
 118
 119
 120def _require_positive_area(
 121    p1: PointType, p2: PointType, p3: PointType, abs_tol: float
 122) -> float:
 123    signed = triangle_signed_area(p1, p2, p3)
 124    if abs(signed) <= abs_tol:
 125        raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
 126    return signed

 129def _closest_point_on_segment(
 130    point: PointType, start: PointType, end: PointType
 131) -> PointType:
 132    start_x, start_y = start[:2]
 133    end_x, end_y = end[:2]
 134    point_x, point_y = point[:2]
 135    delta_x = end_x - start_x
 136    delta_y = end_y - start_y
 137    length_sq = delta_x * delta_x + delta_y * delta_y
 138    if length_sq == 0.0:
 139        return (start_x, start_y)
 140    param = (
 141        (point_x - start_x) * delta_x + (point_y - start_y) * delta_y
 142    ) / length_sq
 143    param = max(0.0, min(1.0, param))
 144    return (start_x + param * delta_x, start_y + param * delta_y)
 145
 146
 147def _unique_points(
 148    points: Sequence[PointType],
 149    rel_tol: float | None = None,
 150    abs_tol: float | None = None,
 151) -> list[PointType]:
 152    unique: list[PointType] = []
 153    for point in points:
 154        xy = _xy(point)
 155        if not any(equal_points(xy, kept, rel_tol, abs_tol) for kept in unique):
 156            unique.append(xy)
 157    return unique
 158
 159
 160def _intersection_from_points(
 161    points: Sequence[PointType],
 162    rel_tol: float | None = None,
 163    abs_tol: float | None = None,
 164) -> TriangleIntersection:
 165    unique = _unique_points(points, rel_tol, abs_tol)
 166    if not unique:
 167        return TriangleIntersection(TriangleIntersectionKind.EMPTY, ())
 168    if len(unique) == 1:
 169        return TriangleIntersection(
 170            TriangleIntersectionKind.POINT, tuple(unique)
 171        )
 172    if len(unique) == 2:
 173        return TriangleIntersection(
 174            TriangleIntersectionKind.SEGMENT, tuple(unique)
 175        )
 176    return TriangleIntersection(TriangleIntersectionKind.POLYGON, tuple(unique))

 179def triangle_signed_area(p1: PointType, p2: PointType, p3: PointType) -> float:
 180    """Return the signed area of triangle ``p1 p2 p3``.
 181
 182    Positive when the vertices are counter-clockwise.
 183
 184    Examples:
 185        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 186        >>> sg.triangle_signed_area((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
 187        1800.0
 188        >>> sg.triangle_signed_area((0, 0), (0, 60), (60, 0))
 189        -1800.0
 190    """
 191    return double_area3(p1, p2, p3) / 2.0
 192
 193
 194def triangle_area(p1: PointType, p2: PointType, p3: PointType) -> float:
 195    """Return the unsigned area of triangle ``p1 p2 p3``.
 196
 197    Examples:
 198        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 199        >>> sg.triangle_area((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
 200        1800.0
 201        >>> sg.triangle_area((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 80))
 202        2400.0
 203    """
 204    return abs(triangle_signed_area(p1, p2, p3))

 220def triangle_longest_edge(
 221    p1: PointType, p2: PointType, p3: PointType
 222) -> tuple[PointType, PointType]:
 223    """Return the longest edge as a pair of vertices.
 224
 225    Edges are ``(p1, p2)``, ``(p2, p3)``, ``(p3, p1)``. If two edges have
 226    the same length, the first of those in that order is returned.
 227
 228    Examples:
 229        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 230        >>> sg.triangle_longest_edge((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 80))
 231        ((60.0, 0.0), (0.0, 80.0))
 232    """
 233    return max(_triangle_edges(p1, p2, p3), key=lambda edge: distance(*edge))
 234
 235
 236def triangle_shortest_edge(
 237    p1: PointType, p2: PointType, p3: PointType
 238) -> tuple[PointType, PointType]:
 239    """Return the shortest edge as a pair of vertices.
 240
 241    Edges are ``(p1, p2)``, ``(p2, p3)``, ``(p3, p1)``. If two edges have
 242    the same length, the first of those in that order is returned.
 243
 244    Examples:
 245        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 246        >>> sg.triangle_shortest_edge((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 80))
 247        ((0.0, 0.0), (60.0, 0.0))
 248    """
 249    return min(_triangle_edges(p1, p2, p3), key=lambda edge: distance(*edge))

 252def triangle_opposite_edge(
 253    p1: PointType,
 254    p2: PointType,
 255    p3: PointType,
 256    vertex_index: PointType | int,
 257) -> tuple[PointType, PointType]:
 258    """Return the edge opposite a vertex or vertex index.
 259
 260    Index ``0`` is ``p1`` (opposite ``(p2, p3)``), ``1`` is ``p2``
 261    (opposite ``(p3, p1)``), and ``2`` is ``p3`` (opposite ``(p1, p2)``).
 262
 263    Examples:
 264        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 265        >>> sg.triangle_opposite_edge((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 80), 0)
 266        ((60.0, 0.0), (0.0, 80.0))
 267        >>> sg.triangle_opposite_edge((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 80), (60, 0))
 268        ((0.0, 80.0), (0.0, 0.0))
 269    """
 270    p1, p2, p3 = _xy(p1), _xy(p2), _xy(p3)
 271    if vertex_index in (0, p1) or (
 272        not isinstance(vertex_index, int) and equal_points(vertex_index, p1)
 273    ):
 274        return (p2, p3)
 275    if vertex_index in (1, p2) or (
 276        not isinstance(vertex_index, int) and equal_points(vertex_index, p2)
 277    ):
 278        return (p3, p1)
 279    if vertex_index in (2, p3) or (
 280        not isinstance(vertex_index, int) and equal_points(vertex_index, p3)
 281    ):
 282        return (p1, p2)
 283    if isinstance(vertex_index, int):
 284        raise ValueError("vertex index must be 0, 1, or 2.")
 285    raise ValueError("vertex is not a vertex of this triangle.")
 286

 288def triangle_perimeter(p1: PointType, p2: PointType, p3: PointType) -> float:
 289    """Return the perimeter of triangle ``p1 p2 p3``.
 290
 291    Examples:
 292        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 293        >>> sg.triangle_perimeter((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 80))
 294        240.0
 295    """
 296    side_a, side_b, side_c = _side_lengths(p1, p2, p3)
 297    return side_a + side_b + side_c

 313def triangle_altitudes(
 314    p1: PointType, p2: PointType, p3: PointType
 315) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
 316    """Return altitude lengths to the sides opposite ``p1``, ``p2``, ``p3``.
 317
 318    Examples:
 319        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 320        >>> sg.triangle_altitudes((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 80))
 321        (48.0, 60.0, 80.0)
 322    """
 323    area = triangle_area(p1, p2, p3)
 324    side_a, side_b, side_c = _side_lengths(p1, p2, p3)
 325    if side_a == 0.0 or side_b == 0.0 or side_c == 0.0:
 326        raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
 327    return (2.0 * area / side_a, 2.0 * area / side_b, 2.0 * area / side_c)
 328
 329
 330def triangle_medians(
 331    p1: PointType, p2: PointType, p3: PointType
 332) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
 333    """Return median lengths from ``p1``, ``p2``, and ``p3``.
 334
 335    Examples:
 336        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 337        >>> medians = sg.triangle_medians((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
 338        >>> tuple(round(length, 10) for length in medians)
 339        (42.4264068712, 67.082039325, 67.082039325)
 340    """
 341    side_a, side_b, side_c = _side_lengths(p1, p2, p3)
 342
 343    def median_length(opp: float, adj_b: float, adj_c: float) -> float:
 344        return 0.5 * sqrt(2.0 * adj_b * adj_b + 2.0 * adj_c * adj_c - opp * opp)
 345
 346    return (
 347        median_length(side_a, side_b, side_c),
 348        median_length(side_b, side_a, side_c),
 349        median_length(side_c, side_a, side_b),
 350    )
 351

 418def triangle_2sides_angle(side1: float, angle: float, side2: float) -> Triangle:
 419    """Return a triangle from two sides and the included angle (SAS).
 420
 421    The included-angle vertex is at the origin. ``side1`` lies along the
 422    positive x-axis. ``side2`` is placed at ``angle`` from that axis, so a
 423    positive ``angle`` yields a counterclockwise triangle.
 424
 425    Args:
 426        side1: Length of the side from the origin along the positive x-axis.
 427        angle: Included angle at the origin, in radians.
 428        side2: Length of the side from the origin at ``angle``.
 429
 430    Returns:
 431        Triangle: Vertices at the origin, along the x-axis, and at ``angle``.
 432
 433    Examples:
 434        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 435        >>> tri = sg.triangle_2sides_angle(60, sg.pi / 2, 80)
 436        >>> tri.vertices
 437        ((0.0, 0.0), (60.0, 0.0), (0.0, 80.0))
 438        >>> tri.side_lengths()
 439        (100.0, 80.0, 60.0)
 440    """
 441    if side1 <= 0.0 or side2 <= 0.0:
 442        raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
 443    if not (0.0 < angle < pi):
 444        raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
 445    _, abs_tol = resolve_tol()
 446    p1 = (0.0, 0.0)
 447    p2 = (float(side1) + 0.0, 0.0)
 448    p3_x = side2 * cos(angle) + 0.0
 449    p3_y = side2 * sin(angle) + 0.0
 450    if abs(p3_x) <= abs_tol:
 451        p3_x = 0.0
 452    if abs(p3_y) <= abs_tol:
 453        p3_y = 0.0
 454    p3 = (p3_x, p3_y)
 455    _require_positive_area(p1, p2, p3, abs_tol)
 456    return Triangle(p1, p2, p3)
 457

 459def triangle_2angles_side(
 460    angle_a: float, angle_b: float, side_a: float
 461) -> Triangle:
 462    """Return a triangle from two angles and the included side (ASA).
 463
 464    The vertex of ``angle_a`` is at the origin. The included side (between
 465    that vertex and the vertex of ``angle_b``) lies along the positive
 466    x-axis and has length ``side_a``. A positive construction yields a
 467    counterclockwise triangle.
 468
 469    Args:
 470        angle_a: Interior angle at the origin, in radians.
 471        angle_b: Interior angle at the positive-x vertex, in radians.
 472        side_a: Length of the included side, along the positive x-axis.
 473
 474    Returns:
 475        Triangle: Vertices at the origin, along the x-axis, and at ``angle_a``.
 476
 477    Examples:
 478        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 479        >>> tri = sg.triangle_2angles_side(sg.pi / 2, sg.pi / 4, 60)
 480        >>> tri.vertices
 481        ((0.0, 0.0), (60.0, 0.0), (0.0, 60.0))
 482        >>> tuple(round(angle, 10) for angle in tri.angles())
 483        (1.5707963268, 0.7853981634, 0.7853981634)
 484    """
 485    if side_a <= 0.0:
 486        raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
 487    if not (0.0 < angle_a < pi) or not (0.0 < angle_b < pi):
 488        raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
 489    angle_c = pi - angle_a - angle_b
 490    if not (0.0 < angle_c < pi):
 491        raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
 492    side_b = law_of_sines_side(side_a, angle_c, angle_b)
 493    return triangle_2sides_angle(side_a, angle_a, side_b)
 494
 495
 496def law_of_cosines_side(side_b: float, side_c: float, angle_a: float) -> float:
 497    """Return the side opposite ``angle_a`` from two sides and the included angle.
 498
 499    Examples:
 500        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 501        >>> sg.law_of_cosines_side(60, 80, sg.pi / 2)
 502        100.0
 503    """
 504    return sqrt(
 505        side_b * side_b + side_c * side_c - 2.0 * side_b * side_c * cos(angle_a)
 506    )
 507
 508
 509def law_of_cosines_angle(side_a: float, side_b: float, side_c: float) -> float:
 510    """Return the angle opposite ``side_a`` from three side lengths.
 511
 512    Examples:
 513        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 514        >>> sg.law_of_cosines_angle(100, 80, 60) == sg.pi / 2
 515        True
 516    """
 517    denom = 2.0 * side_b * side_c
 518    if denom == 0.0:
 519        raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
 520    cosine = (side_b * side_b + side_c * side_c - side_a * side_a) / denom
 521    cosine = max(-1.0, min(1.0, cosine))
 522    return acos(cosine)
 523
 524
 525def law_of_sines_side(side_a: float, angle_a: float, angle_b: float) -> float:
 526    """Return the side opposite ``angle_b`` from one side and two angles.
 527
 528    Examples:
 529        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 530        >>> round(sg.law_of_sines_side(60, sg.pi / 2, sg.pi / 6), 10)
 531        30.0
 532    """
 533    if isclose(sin(angle_a), 0.0, rel_tol=0.0, abs_tol=1e-15):
 534        raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
 535    return side_a * sin(angle_b) / sin(angle_a)
 536
 537
 538def is_collinear(
 539    p1: PointType,
 540    p2: PointType,
 541    p3: PointType,
 542    rel_tol: float | None = None,
 543    abs_tol: float | None = None,
 544) -> bool:
 545    """Return True if ``p1``, ``p2``, and ``p3`` are collinear.
 546
 547    Examples:
 548        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 549        >>> sg.is_collinear((0, 0), (40, 40), (80, 80))
 550        True
 551        >>> sg.is_collinear((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
 552        False
 553    """
 554    return collinear3(p1, p2, p3, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol)
 555
 556
 557def is_degenerate_triangle(
 558    p1: PointType,
 559    p2: PointType,
 560    p3: PointType,
 561    rel_tol: float | None = None,
 562    abs_tol: float | None = None,
 563) -> bool:
 564    """Return True if the three points do not form a triangle of positive area.
 565
 566    Examples:
 567        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 568        >>> sg.is_degenerate_triangle((0, 0), (40, 0), (80, 0))
 569        True
 570        >>> sg.is_degenerate_triangle((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
 571        False
 572    """
 573    _, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
 574    return abs(triangle_signed_area(p1, p2, p3)) <= abs_tol
 575
 576
 577def is_valid_triangle(
 578    p1: PointType,
 579    p2: PointType,
 580    p3: PointType,
 581    rel_tol: float | None = None,
 582    abs_tol: float | None = None,
 583) -> bool:
 584    """Return True if ``p1 p2 p3`` has positive area.
 585
 586    Examples:
 587        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 588        >>> sg.is_valid_triangle((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
 589        True
 590        >>> sg.is_valid_triangle((0, 0), (40, 0), (80, 0))
 591        False
 592    """
 593    return not is_degenerate_triangle(p1, p2, p3, rel_tol, abs_tol)
 594
 595
 596def is_equilateral_triangle(
 597    p1: PointType,
 598    p2: PointType,
 599    p3: PointType,
 600    rel_tol: float | None = None,
 601    abs_tol: float | None = None,
 602) -> bool:
 603    """Return True if all three sides are equal within tolerance.
 604
 605    Examples:
 606        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 607        >>> sg.is_equilateral_triangle((0, 0), (60, 0), (30, 51.9615242268))
 608        True
 609        >>> sg.is_equilateral_triangle((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
 610        False
 611    """
 612    rel_tol, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
 613    side_a, side_b, side_c = _side_lengths(p1, p2, p3)
 614    return isclose(
 615        side_a, side_b, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol
 616    ) and isclose(side_b, side_c, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol)
 617
 618
 619def is_isosceles_triangle(
 620    p1: PointType,
 621    p2: PointType,
 622    p3: PointType,
 623    rel_tol: float | None = None,
 624    abs_tol: float | None = None,
 625) -> bool:
 626    """Return True if at least two sides are equal within tolerance.
 627
 628    Examples:
 629        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 630        >>> sg.is_isosceles_triangle((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
 631        True
 632        >>> sg.is_isosceles_triangle((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 80))
 633        False
 634    """
 635    rel_tol, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
 636    side_a, side_b, side_c = _side_lengths(p1, p2, p3)
 637    return (
 638        isclose(side_a, side_b, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol)
 639        or isclose(side_b, side_c, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol)
 640        or isclose(side_c, side_a, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol)
 641    )
 642
 643
 644def is_scalene_triangle(
 645    p1: PointType,
 646    p2: PointType,
 647    p3: PointType,
 648    rel_tol: float | None = None,
 649    abs_tol: float | None = None,
 650) -> bool:
 651    """Return True if no two sides are equal within tolerance.
 652
 653    Examples:
 654        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 655        >>> sg.is_scalene_triangle((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 80))
 656        True
 657        >>> sg.is_scalene_triangle((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
 658        False
 659    """
 660    return is_valid_triangle(p1, p2, p3, rel_tol, abs_tol) and not (
 661        is_isosceles_triangle(p1, p2, p3, rel_tol, abs_tol)
 662    )
 663
 664
 665def is_right_triangle(
 666    p1: PointType,
 667    p2: PointType,
 668    p3: PointType,
 669    rel_tol: float | None = None,
 670    abs_tol: float | None = None,
 671) -> bool:
 672    """Return True if one angle is a right angle within tolerance.
 673
 674    Examples:
 675        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 676        >>> sg.is_right_triangle((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 80))
 677        True
 678        >>> sg.is_right_triangle((0, 0), (60, 0), (30, 60))
 679        False
 680    """
 681    rel_tol, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
 682    sides = sorted(_side_lengths(p1, p2, p3))
 683    return isclose(
 684        sides[0] * sides[0] + sides[1] * sides[1],
 685        sides[2] * sides[2],
 686        rel_tol=rel_tol,
 687        abs_tol=abs_tol,
 688    )
 689
 690
 691def is_acute_triangle(
 692    p1: PointType,
 693    p2: PointType,
 694    p3: PointType,
 695    rel_tol: float | None = None,
 696    abs_tol: float | None = None,
 697) -> bool:
 698    """Return True if all angles are acute.
 699
 700    Examples:
 701        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 702        >>> sg.is_acute_triangle((0, 0), (60, 0), (30, 60))
 703        True
 704        >>> sg.is_acute_triangle((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 80))
 705        False
 706    """
 707    rel_tol, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
 708    if is_degenerate_triangle(p1, p2, p3, rel_tol, abs_tol):
 709        return False
 710    sides = sorted(_side_lengths(p1, p2, p3))
 711    return (
 712        sides[0] * sides[0] + sides[1] * sides[1]
 713        > sides[2] * sides[2] + abs_tol
 714    )
 715
 716
 717def is_obtuse_triangle(
 718    p1: PointType,
 719    p2: PointType,
 720    p3: PointType,
 721    rel_tol: float | None = None,
 722    abs_tol: float | None = None,
 723) -> bool:
 724    """Return True if one angle is obtuse.
 725
 726    Examples:
 727        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 728        >>> sg.is_obtuse_triangle((0, 0), (20, 0), (60, 2))
 729        True
 730        >>> sg.is_obtuse_triangle((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 80))
 731        False
 732    """
 733    rel_tol, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
 734    if is_degenerate_triangle(p1, p2, p3, rel_tol, abs_tol):
 735        return False
 736    sides = sorted(_side_lengths(p1, p2, p3))
 737    return (
 738        sides[0] * sides[0] + sides[1] * sides[1]
 739        < sides[2] * sides[2] - abs_tol
 740    )
 741
 742
 743def triangle_orientation(
 744    p1: PointType,
 745    p2: PointType,
 746    p3: PointType,
 747    rel_tol: float | None = None,
 748    abs_tol: float | None = None,
 749) -> int:
 750    """Return ``1`` if CCW, ``-1`` if CW, ``0`` if collinear.
 751
 752    Examples:
 753        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 754        >>> sg.triangle_orientation((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
 755        1
 756        >>> sg.triangle_orientation((0, 0), (0, 60), (60, 0))
 757        -1
 758        >>> sg.triangle_orientation((0, 0), (40, 0), (80, 0))
 759        0
 760    """
 761    _, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
 762    signed = triangle_signed_area(p1, p2, p3)
 763    if abs(signed) <= abs_tol:
 764        return 0
 765    if signed > 0:
 766        return 1
 767    return -1
 768
 769
 770def is_counterclockwise(
 771    p1: PointType,
 772    p2: PointType,
 773    p3: PointType,
 774    rel_tol: float | None = None,
 775    abs_tol: float | None = None,
 776) -> bool:
 777    """Return True if ``p1 p2 p3`` is counter-clockwise.
 778
 779    Examples:
 780        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 781        >>> sg.is_counterclockwise((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
 782        True
 783    """
 784    return triangle_orientation(p1, p2, p3, rel_tol, abs_tol) == 1

 787def is_clockwise(
 788    p1: PointType,
 789    p2: PointType,
 790    p3: PointType,
 791    rel_tol: float | None = None,
 792    abs_tol: float | None = None,
 793) -> bool:
 794    """Return True if ``p1 p2 p3`` is clockwise.
 795
 796    Examples:
 797        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 798        >>> sg.is_clockwise((0, 0), (0, 60), (60, 0))
 799        True
 800    """
 801    return triangle_orientation(p1, p2, p3, rel_tol, abs_tol) == -1

 804def reverse_winding(triangle: TriangleLike) -> Triangle:
 805    """Return a new ``Triangle`` with reversed vertex order.
 806
 807    Examples:
 808        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 809        >>> tri = sg.reverse_winding(((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60)))
 810        >>> tri.vertices
 811        ((0.0, 60.0), (60.0, 0.0), (0.0, 0.0))
 812    """
 813    p1, p2, p3 = _triangle_vertices(triangle)
 814    return Triangle(p3, p2, p1)

 816
 817def triangle_centroid(p1: PointType, p2: PointType, p3: PointType) -> PointType:
 818    """Return the centroid of triangle ``p1 p2 p3``.
 819
 820    Examples:
 821        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 822        >>> sg.triangle_centroid((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
 823        (20.0, 20.0)
 824    """
 825    return triangle_centroid3(p1, p2, p3)
 826
 827
 828def triangle_incenter(p1: PointType, p2: PointType, p3: PointType) -> PointType:
 829    """Return the incenter of triangle ``p1 p2 p3``.
 830
 831    Examples:
 832        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 833        >>> sg.triangle_incenter((0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 60))
 834        (20.0, 20.0)
 835    """
 836    side_a, side_b, side_c = _side_lengths(p1, p2, p3)
 837    perimeter = side_a + side_b + side_c
 838    if perimeter == 0.0:
 839        raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
 840    x1, y1 = p1[:2]
 841    x2, y2 = p2[:2]
 842    x3, y3 = p3[:2]
 843    center_x = (side_a * x1 + side_b * x2 + side_c * x3) / perimeter
 844    center_y = (side_a * y1 + side_b * y2 + side_c * y3) / perimeter
 845    return (center_x, center_y)
 846
 847
 848def triangle_circumcenter(
 849    p1: PointType, p2: PointType, p3: PointType
 850) -> PointType:
 851    """Return the circumcenter of triangle ``p1 p2 p3``.
 852
 853    Examples:
 854        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 855        >>> sg.triangle_circumcenter((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
 856        (30.0, 30.0)
 857    """
 858    bisector_ab = perp_bisector((p1, p2))
 859    bisector_ac = perp_bisector((p1, p3))
 860    center = intersect(bisector_ab, bisector_ac)
 861    if center is None:
 862        raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
 863    return _xy(center)
 864
 865
 866def triangle_orthocenter(
 867    p1: PointType, p2: PointType, p3: PointType
 868) -> PointType:
 869    """Return the orthocenter of triangle ``p1 p2 p3``.
 870
 871    Examples:
 872        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 873        >>> sg.triangle_orthocenter((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
 874        (0.0, 0.0)
 875    """
 876    centroid_x, centroid_y = triangle_centroid(p1, p2, p3)
 877    circum_x, circum_y = triangle_circumcenter(p1, p2, p3)
 878    return (
 879        3.0 * centroid_x - 2.0 * circum_x,
 880        3.0 * centroid_y - 2.0 * circum_y,
 881    )
 882
 883
 884def triangle_nine_point_center(
 885    p1: PointType, p2: PointType, p3: PointType
 886) -> PointType:
 887    """Return the nine-point center of triangle ``p1 p2 p3``.
 888
 889    Examples:
 890        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 891        >>> sg.triangle_nine_point_center((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
 892        (15.0, 15.0)
 893    """
 894    circum = triangle_circumcenter(p1, p2, p3)
 895    ortho = triangle_orthocenter(p1, p2, p3)
 896    return midpoint(circum, ortho)
 897
 898
 899def triangle_excenters(
 900    p1: PointType, p2: PointType, p3: PointType
 901) -> tuple[PointType, PointType, PointType]:
 902    """Return the three excenters opposite ``p1``, ``p2``, and ``p3``.
 903
 904    Examples:
 905        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 906        >>> centers = sg.triangle_excenters((0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 60))
 907        >>> tuple(tuple(round(coord, 10) for coord in center) for center in centers)
 908        ((120.0, 120.0), (-40.0, 40.0), (60.0, -60.0))
 909    """
 910    side_a, side_b, side_c = _side_lengths(p1, p2, p3)
 911    x1, y1 = p1[:2]
 912    x2, y2 = p2[:2]
 913    x3, y3 = p3[:2]
 914
 915    def excenter(
 916        opp: float,
 917        adj_b: float,
 918        adj_c: float,
 919        px: float,
 920        py: float,
 921        qx: float,
 922        qy: float,
 923        rx: float,
 924        ry: float,
 925    ) -> PointType:
 926        denom = -opp + adj_b + adj_c
 927        if denom == 0.0:
 928            raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
 929        center_x = (-opp * px + adj_b * qx + adj_c * rx) / denom
 930        center_y = (-opp * py + adj_b * qy + adj_c * ry) / denom
 931        return (center_x, center_y)
 932
 933    return (
 934        excenter(side_a, side_b, side_c, x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3),
 935        excenter(side_b, side_a, side_c, x2, y2, x1, y1, x3, y3),
 936        excenter(side_c, side_a, side_b, x3, y3, x1, y1, x2, y2),
 937    )
 938
 939
 940def triangle_inradius(p1: PointType, p2: PointType, p3: PointType) -> float:
 941    """Return the inradius of triangle ``p1 p2 p3``.
 942
 943    Examples:
 944        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 945        >>> sg.triangle_inradius((0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 60))
 946        20.0
 947    """
 948    semiperimeter = triangle_semiperimeter(p1, p2, p3)
 949    if semiperimeter == 0.0:
 950        raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
 951    return triangle_area(p1, p2, p3) / semiperimeter
 952
 953
 954def triangle_circumradius(p1: PointType, p2: PointType, p3: PointType) -> float:
 955    """Return the circumradius of triangle ``p1 p2 p3``.
 956
 957    Examples:
 958        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 959        >>> sg.triangle_circumradius((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
 960        42.42640687119285
 961    """
 962    return distance(triangle_circumcenter(p1, p2, p3), p1)
 963
 964
 965def triangle_incircle(triangle: TriangleLike) -> Circle:
 966    """Return the incircle of ``triangle``.
 967
 968    Examples:
 969        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 970        >>> circle = sg.triangle_incircle(((0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 60)))
 971        >>> tuple(round(float(coord), 10) for coord in circle.center[:2])
 972        (20.0, 20.0)
 973        >>> circle.radius
 974        20.0
 975    """
 976    p1, p2, p3 = _triangle_vertices(triangle)
 977    return Circle(
 978        radius=triangle_inradius(p1, p2, p3),
 979        center=triangle_incenter(p1, p2, p3),
 980    )

 982
 983def triangle_circumcircle(triangle: TriangleLike) -> Circle:
 984    """Return the circumcircle of ``triangle``.
 985
 986    Examples:
 987        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 988        >>> circle = sg.triangle_circumcircle(((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60)))
 989        >>> tuple(circle.center[:2])
 990        (30.0, 30.0)
 991    """

 993    return Circle(
 994        radius=triangle_circumradius(p1, p2, p3),
 995        center=triangle_circumcenter(p1, p2, p3),
 996    )

 998
 999def triangle_nine_point_circle(triangle: TriangleLike) -> Circle:
1000    """Return the nine-point circle of ``triangle``.
1001
1002    Examples:
1003        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1004        >>> circle = sg.triangle_nine_point_circle(((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60)))
1005        >>> tuple(circle.center[:2])
1006        (15.0, 15.0)
1007    """
1008    p1, p2, p3 = _triangle_vertices(triangle)
1009    return Circle(
1010        radius=triangle_circumradius(p1, p2, p3) / 2.0,
1011        center=triangle_nine_point_center(p1, p2, p3),
1012    )

1014
1015def barycentric_coordinates(
1016    point: PointType, triangle: TriangleLike
1017) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
1018    """Return barycentric weights of ``point`` with respect to ``triangle``.
1019
1020    Examples:
1021        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1022        >>> sg.barycentric_coordinates((0, 0), ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60)))
1023        (1.0, 0.0, 0.0)
1024        >>> sg.barycentric_coordinates((30, 30), ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60)))
1025        (0.0, 0.5, 0.5)
1026    """
1027    p1, p2, p3 = _triangle_vertices(triangle)
1028    area = triangle_signed_area(p1, p2, p3)
1029    if area == 0.0:
1030        raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
1031    weight1 = triangle_signed_area(point, p2, p3) / area
1032    weight2 = triangle_signed_area(p1, point, p3) / area
1033    weight3 = triangle_signed_area(p1, p2, point) / area
1034    return (weight1, weight2, weight3)
1035
1036
1037def cartesian_from_barycentric(
1038    weights: Sequence[float], triangle: TriangleLike
1039) -> PointType:
1040    """Return the Cartesian point for barycentric ``weights``.
1041
1042    Examples:
1043        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1044        >>> sg.cartesian_from_barycentric((1, 0, 0), ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60)))
1045        (0.0, 0.0)
1046        >>> sg.cartesian_from_barycentric((0, 0.5, 0.5), ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60)))
1047        (30.0, 30.0)
1048    """
1049    p1, p2, p3 = _triangle_vertices(triangle)
1050    w1, w2, w3 = weights[:3]
1051    x1, y1 = p1[:2]
1052    x2, y2 = p2[:2]
1053    x3, y3 = p3[:2]
1054    return (w1 * x1 + w2 * x2 + w3 * x3, w1 * y1 + w2 * y2 + w3 * y3)
1055
1056
1057def is_valid_barycentric(
1058    weights: Sequence[float],
1059    rel_tol: float | None = None,
1060    abs_tol: float | None = None,
1061) -> bool:
1062    """Return True if ``weights`` sum to 1 within tolerance.
1063
1064    Examples:
1065        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1066        >>> sg.is_valid_barycentric((0.2, 0.3, 0.5))
1067        True
1068        >>> sg.is_valid_barycentric((1, 1, 1))
1069        False
1070    """
1071    rel_tol, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
1072    return isclose(sum(weights[:3]), 1.0, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol)
1073
1074
1075def normalize_barycentric(
1076    weights: Sequence[float],
1077) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
1078    """Return ``weights`` scaled so they sum to 1.
1079
1080    Examples:
1081        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1082        >>> sg.normalize_barycentric((1, 1, 2))
1083        (0.25, 0.25, 0.5)
1084    """
1085    w1, w2, w3 = weights[:3]
1086    total = w1 + w2 + w3
1087    if total == 0.0:
1088        raise ValueError("Cannot normalize barycentric weights that sum to 0.")
1089    return (w1 / total, w2 / total, w3 / total)
1090
1091
1092def interpolate_triangle(
1093    values: Sequence[Any], barycentric_weights: Sequence[float]
1094) -> Any:
1095    """Interpolate three vertex values with barycentric weights.
1096
1097    Examples:
1098        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1099        >>> sg.interpolate_triangle((0, 40, 80), (0.5, 0.5, 0))
1100        20.0
1101    """
1102    w1, w2, w3 = barycentric_weights[:3]
1103    v1, v2, v3 = values[:3]
1104    return w1 * v1 + w2 * v2 + w3 * v3
1105
1106
1107def interpolate_triangle_at_point(
1108    point: PointType, triangle: TriangleLike, values: Sequence[Any]
1109) -> Any:
1110    """Interpolate ``values`` at ``point`` on ``triangle``.
1111
1112    Examples:
1113        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1114        >>> sg.interpolate_triangle_at_point(
1115        ...     (0, 0), ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60)), (30, 40, 50)
1116        ... )
1117        30.0
1118    """
1119    return interpolate_triangle(
1120        values, barycentric_coordinates(point, triangle)
1121    )
1122
1123
1124def triangle_contains_point_inclusive(
1125    triangle: TriangleLike,
1126    point: PointType,
1127    rel_tol: float | None = None,
1128    abs_tol: float | None = None,
1129) -> bool:
1130    """Return True if ``point`` is inside ``triangle`` or on its boundary.
1131
1132    Examples:
1133        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1134        >>> tri = ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
1135        >>> sg.triangle_contains_point_inclusive(tri, (20, 20))
1136        True
1137        >>> sg.triangle_contains_point_inclusive(tri, (0, 0))
1138        True
1139        >>> sg.triangle_contains_point_inclusive(tri, (80, 80))
1140        False
1141    """
1142    rel_tol, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
1143    p1, p2, p3 = _triangle_vertices(triangle)
1144    if is_degenerate_triangle(p1, p2, p3, rel_tol, abs_tol):
1145        return False
1146    w1, w2, w3 = barycentric_coordinates(point, (p1, p2, p3))
1147    return (
1148        w1 >= -abs_tol
1149        and w2 >= -abs_tol
1150        and w3 >= -abs_tol
1151        and isclose(w1 + w2 + w3, 1.0, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol)
1152    )
1153
1154
1155def triangle_contains_point_strictly(
1156    triangle: TriangleLike,
1157    point: PointType,
1158    rel_tol: float | None = None,
1159    abs_tol: float | None = None,
1160) -> bool:
1161    """Return True if ``point`` is strictly inside ``triangle``.
1162
1163    Examples:
1164        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1165        >>> tri = ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
1166        >>> sg.triangle_contains_point_strictly(tri, (20, 20))
1167        True
1168        >>> sg.triangle_contains_point_strictly(tri, (0, 0))
1169        False
1170    """
1171    rel_tol, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
1172    p1, p2, p3 = _triangle_vertices(triangle)
1173    if is_degenerate_triangle(p1, p2, p3, rel_tol, abs_tol):
1174        return False
1175    w1, w2, w3 = barycentric_coordinates(point, (p1, p2, p3))
1176    return w1 > abs_tol and w2 > abs_tol and w3 > abs_tol
1177
1178
1179def triangle_contains_point(
1180    triangle: TriangleLike,
1181    point: PointType,
1182    rel_tol: float | None = None,
1183    abs_tol: float | None = None,
1184) -> bool:
1185    """Return True if ``point`` is inside ``triangle`` or on its boundary.
1186
1187    Examples:
1188        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1189        >>> sg.triangle_contains_point(((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60)), (20, 20))
1190        True
1191    """
1192    return triangle_contains_point_inclusive(triangle, point, rel_tol, abs_tol)
1193
1194
1195def classify_point_in_triangle(
1196    triangle: TriangleLike,
1197    point: PointType,
1198    rel_tol: float | None = None,
1199    abs_tol: float | None = None,
1200) -> TrianglePointClass:
1201    """Classify ``point`` relative to ``triangle``.
1202
1203    Examples:
1204        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1205        >>> tri = ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
1206        >>> sg.classify_point_in_triangle(tri, (20, 20))
1207        <TrianglePointClass.INSIDE: 'Inside'>
1208        >>> sg.classify_point_in_triangle(tri, (0, 0))
1209        <TrianglePointClass.ON_VERTEX: 'OnVertex'>
1210        >>> sg.classify_point_in_triangle(tri, (30, 0))
1211        <TrianglePointClass.ON_EDGE: 'OnEdge'>
1212        >>> sg.classify_point_in_triangle(tri, (80, 80))
1213        <TrianglePointClass.OUTSIDE: 'Outside'>
1214    """
1215    rel_tol, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
1216    p1, p2, p3 = _triangle_vertices(triangle)
1217    if is_degenerate_triangle(p1, p2, p3, rel_tol, abs_tol):
1218        return TrianglePointClass.DEGENERATE
1219    if (
1220        equal_points(point, p1, rel_tol, abs_tol)
1221        or equal_points(point, p2, rel_tol, abs_tol)
1222        or equal_points(point, p3, rel_tol, abs_tol)
1223    ):
1224        return TrianglePointClass.ON_VERTEX
1225    if (
1226        on_segment(p1, p2, point, eps=abs_tol)
1227        or on_segment(p2, p3, point, eps=abs_tol)
1228        or on_segment(p3, p1, point, eps=abs_tol)
1229    ):
1230        return TrianglePointClass.ON_EDGE
1231    if triangle_contains_point_strictly(triangle, point, rel_tol, abs_tol):
1232        return TrianglePointClass.INSIDE
1233    return TrianglePointClass.OUTSIDE
1234
1235
1236def closest_point_on_triangle(
1237    point: PointType, triangle: TriangleLike
1238) -> PointType:
1239    """Return the closest point of ``triangle`` to ``point``.
1240
1241    Examples:
1242        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1243        >>> sg.closest_point_on_triangle((20, 20), ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60)))
1244        (20.0, 20.0)
1245        >>> sg.closest_point_on_triangle((80, 0), ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60)))
1246        (60.0, 0.0)
1247    """
1248    p1, p2, p3 = _triangle_vertices(triangle)
1249    if triangle_contains_point_inclusive((p1, p2, p3), point):
1250        return _xy(point)
1251    candidates = (
1252        _closest_point_on_segment(point, p1, p2),
1253        _closest_point_on_segment(point, p2, p3),
1254        _closest_point_on_segment(point, p3, p1),
1255    )
1256    return min(candidates, key=lambda candidate: distance(point, candidate))
1257
1258
1259def distance_to_triangle(point: PointType, triangle: TriangleLike) -> float:
1260    """Return the distance from ``point`` to ``triangle``.
1261
1262    Examples:
1263        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1264        >>> sg.distance_to_triangle((20, 20), ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60)))
1265        0.0
1266        >>> sg.distance_to_triangle((80, 0), ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60)))
1267        20.0
1268    """
1269    return distance(point, closest_point_on_triangle(point, triangle))
1270
1271
1272def _ray_param(
1273    origin: PointType, direction: PointType, point: PointType
1274) -> float:
1275    origin_x, origin_y = origin[:2]
1276    dir_x, dir_y = direction[:2]
1277    point_x, point_y = point[:2]
1278    denom = dir_x * dir_x + dir_y * dir_y
1279    if denom == 0.0:
1280        return 0.0
1281    return ((point_x - origin_x) * dir_x + (point_y - origin_y) * dir_y) / denom
1282
1283
1284def _edge_hits_with_line(
1285    line: LineType, triangle: TriangleLike
1286) -> list[PointType]:
1287    p1, p2, p3 = _triangle_vertices(triangle)
1288    hits: list[PointType] = []
1289    for edge in ((p1, p2), (p2, p3), (p3, p1)):
1290        hit = intersect(line, edge)
1291        if hit is None:
1292            continue
1293        if on_segment(edge[0], edge[1], hit):
1294            hits.append(_xy(hit))
1295    return hits
1296
1297
1298def intersect_line_triangle(
1299    line: LineType, triangle: TriangleLike
1300) -> TriangleIntersection:
1301    """Intersect an infinite line with ``triangle``.
1302
1303    Examples:
1304        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1305        >>> hit = sg.intersect_line_triangle([(0, 15), (60, 15)], ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60)))
1306        >>> hit.kind
1307        <TriangleIntersectionKind.SEGMENT: 'A segment'>
1308        >>> hit.points
1309        ((45.0, 15.0), (0.0, 15.0))
1310    """
1311    return _intersection_from_points(_edge_hits_with_line(line, triangle))
1312
1313
1314def intersect_segment_triangle(
1315    segment: LineType, triangle: TriangleLike
1316) -> TriangleIntersection:
1317    """Intersect a line segment with ``triangle``.
1318
1319    Examples:
1320        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1321        >>> hit = sg.intersect_segment_triangle(
1322        ...     [(-60, 15), (60, 15)], ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
1323        ... )
1324        >>> hit.kind
1325        <TriangleIntersectionKind.SEGMENT: 'A segment'>
1326        >>> hit.points
1327        ((45.0, 15.0), (0.0, 15.0))
1328    """
1329    p1, p2, p3 = _triangle_vertices(triangle)
1330    start, end = _xy(segment[0]), _xy(segment[1])
1331    points: list[PointType] = []
1332    if triangle_contains_point_inclusive((p1, p2, p3), start):
1333        points.append(start)
1334    if triangle_contains_point_inclusive((p1, p2, p3), end):
1335        points.append(end)
1336    for edge in ((p1, p2), (p2, p3), (p3, p1)):
1337        kind, hit = intersection((start, end), edge)
1338        if kind == Connection.INTERSECT and hit is not None:
1339            points.append(_xy(hit))
1340    return _intersection_from_points(points)
1341
1342
1343def intersect_ray_triangle(
1344    ray: LineType, triangle: TriangleLike
1345) -> RayTriangleHit | None:
1346    """Intersect a ray with ``triangle``.
1347
1348    ``ray`` is ``(origin, point_on_ray)``. The first hit along the ray is
1349    returned, or ``None`` if the ray misses.
1350
1351    Examples:
1352        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1353        >>> hit = sg.intersect_ray_triangle(
1354        ...     [(-60, 15), (60, 15)], ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
1355        ... )
1356        >>> hit.point
1357        (0.0, 15.0)
1358        >>> hit.distance
1359        60.0
1360        >>> hit.front_facing
1361        True
1362    """
1363    origin = _xy(ray[0])
1364    through = _xy(ray[1])
1365    direction = (through[0] - origin[0], through[1] - origin[1])
1366    p1, p2, p3 = _triangle_vertices(triangle)
1367    _, abs_tol = resolve_tol()
1368    candidates: list[PointType] = []
1369    if triangle_contains_point_inclusive((p1, p2, p3), origin):
1370        candidates.append(origin)
1371    for point in _edge_hits_with_line((origin, through), (p1, p2, p3)):
1372        param = _ray_param(origin, direction, point)
1373        if param >= -abs_tol:
1374            candidates.append(point)
1375    unique = _unique_points(candidates)
1376    if not unique:
1377        return None
1378    hit_point = min(
1379        unique, key=lambda point: _ray_param(origin, direction, point)
1380    )
1381    return RayTriangleHit(
1382        point=hit_point,
1383        distance=distance(origin, hit_point),
1384        barycentric_coordinates=barycentric_coordinates(
1385            hit_point, (p1, p2, p3)
1386        ),
1387        front_facing=is_counterclockwise(p1, p2, p3),
1388    )
1389
1390
1391def _is_left_or_on(
1392    origin: PointType, dest: PointType, point: PointType, abs_tol: float
1393) -> bool:
1394    signed = double_area3(origin, dest, point)
1395    return signed >= -abs_tol * 2.0
1396
1397
1398def _clip_polygon_by_edge(
1399    polygon: Sequence[PointType],
1400    origin: PointType,
1401    dest: PointType,
1402    abs_tol: float,
1403) -> list[PointType]:
1404    if not polygon:
1405        return []
1406    output: list[PointType] = []
1407    prev = polygon[-1]
1408    prev_inside = _is_left_or_on(origin, dest, prev, abs_tol)
1409    for current in polygon:
1410        current_inside = _is_left_or_on(origin, dest, current, abs_tol)
1411        if current_inside:
1412            if not prev_inside:
1413                hit = intersect((prev, current), (origin, dest))
1414                if hit is not None:
1415                    output.append(_xy(hit))
1416            output.append(_xy(current))
1417        elif prev_inside:
1418            hit = intersect((prev, current), (origin, dest))
1419            if hit is not None:
1420                output.append(_xy(hit))
1421        prev = current
1422        prev_inside = current_inside
1423    return output
1424
1425
1426def intersect_triangle_triangle(
1427    triangle1: TriangleLike, triangle2: TriangleLike
1428) -> TriangleIntersection:
1429    """Intersect two triangles.
1430
1431    Examples:
1432        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1433        >>> hit = sg.intersect_triangle_triangle(
1434        ...     ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60)), ((30, -30), (30, 60), (90, 0))
1435        ... )
1436        >>> hit.kind
1437        <TriangleIntersectionKind.POLYGON: 'A polygon'>
1438        >>> hit.points
1439        ((30.0, 30.0), (30.0, 0.0), (60.0, 0.0))
1440    """
1441    _, abs_tol = resolve_tol()
1442    p1, p2, p3 = _triangle_vertices(triangle1)
1443    q1, q2, q3 = _triangle_vertices(triangle2)
1444    clip = [p1, p2, p3]
1445    if triangle_orientation(p1, p2, p3) < 0:
1446        clip = [p1, p3, p2]
1447    subject = [q1, q2, q3]
1448    if triangle_orientation(q1, q2, q3) < 0:
1449        subject = [q1, q3, q2]
1450    for i, origin in enumerate(clip):
1451        dest = clip[(i + 1) % 3]
1452        subject = _clip_polygon_by_edge(subject, origin, dest, abs_tol)
1453        if not subject:
1454            break
1455    return _intersection_from_points(subject)
1456
1457
1458def subdivide_triangle_by_midpoints(
1459    triangle: TriangleLike,
1460) -> tuple[Triangle, Triangle, Triangle, Triangle]:
1461    """Subdivide ``triangle`` into four triangles at the side midpoints.
1462
1463    Examples:
1464        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1465        >>> parts = sg.subdivide_triangle_by_midpoints(((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60)))
1466        >>> len(parts)
1467        4
1468        >>> parts[0].vertices
1469        ((0.0, 0.0), (30.0, 0.0), (0.0, 30.0))
1470    """
1471    p1, p2, p3 = _triangle_vertices(triangle)
1472    m12 = midpoint(p1, p2)
1473    m23 = midpoint(p2, p3)
1474    m31 = midpoint(p3, p1)
1475    return (
1476        Triangle(p1, m12, m31),
1477        Triangle(p2, m23, m12),
1478        Triangle(p3, m31, m23),
1479        Triangle(m12, m23, m31),
1480    )
1481
1482
1483def subdivide_triangle_at_centroid(
1484    triangle: TriangleLike,
1485) -> tuple[Triangle, Triangle, Triangle]:
1486    """Subdivide ``triangle`` into three triangles at the centroid.
1487
1488    Examples:
1489        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1490        >>> parts = sg.subdivide_triangle_at_centroid(((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60)))
1491        >>> len(parts)
1492        3
1493        >>> parts[0].vertices
1494        ((0.0, 0.0), (60.0, 0.0), (20.0, 20.0))
1495    """
1496    p1, p2, p3 = _triangle_vertices(triangle)
1497    center = triangle_centroid(p1, p2, p3)
1498    return (
1499        Triangle(p1, p2, center),
1500        Triangle(p2, p3, center),
1501        Triangle(p3, p1, center),
1502    )
1503
1504
1505def subdivide_triangle_at_point(
1506    triangle: TriangleLike, point: PointType
1507) -> tuple[Triangle, Triangle, Triangle]:
1508    """Subdivide ``triangle`` into three triangles at ``point``.
1509
1510    Examples:
1511        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1512        >>> parts = sg.subdivide_triangle_at_point(((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60)), (15, 15))
1513        >>> len(parts)
1514        3
1515        >>> parts[0].vertices
1516        ((0.0, 0.0), (60.0, 0.0), (15.0, 15.0))
1517    """
1518    p1, p2, p3 = _triangle_vertices(triangle)
1519    if not triangle_contains_point_inclusive((p1, p2, p3), point):
1520        raise ValueError("Point is outside the triangle.")
1521    interior = _xy(point)
1522    return (
1523        Triangle(p1, p2, interior),
1524        Triangle(p2, p3, interior),
1525        Triangle(p3, p1, interior),
1526    )
1527
1528
1529def similar_triangles(
1530    triangle1: TriangleLike,
1531    triangle2: TriangleLike,
1532    rel_tol: float | None = None,
1533    abs_tol: float | None = None,
1534) -> bool:
1535    """Return True if the two triangles have proportional side lengths.
1536
1537    Examples:
1538        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1539        >>> sg.similar_triangles(
1540        ...     ((0, 0), (30, 0), (0, 40)), ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 80))
1541        ... )
1542        True
1543        >>> sg.similar_triangles(
1544        ...     ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 80)), ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
1545        ... )
1546        False
1547    """
1548    rel_tol, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
1549    p1, p2, p3 = _triangle_vertices(triangle1)
1550    q1, q2, q3 = _triangle_vertices(triangle2)
1551    if is_degenerate_triangle(p1, p2, p3) or is_degenerate_triangle(q1, q2, q3):
1552        return False
1553    sides1 = sorted(_side_lengths(p1, p2, p3))
1554    sides2 = sorted(_side_lengths(q1, q2, q3))
1555    if sides1[0] == 0.0 or sides2[0] == 0.0:
1556        return False
1557    ratio = sides1[0] / sides2[0]
1558    return all(
1559        isclose(side1, ratio * side2, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol)
1560        for side1, side2 in zip(sides1, sides2)
1561    )
1562
1563
1564class Triangle(Shape):
1565    """A three-vertex closed shape with triangle geometry helpers.
1566
1567    Methods wrap the module-level ``triangle_*`` functions, the same pattern
1568    as ``Vector`` wrapping ``v_*``.
1569
1570    Examples:
1571        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1572        >>> tri = sg.Triangle((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 80))
1573        >>> tri.area()
1574        2400.0
1575        >>> tri.side_lengths()
1576        (100.0, 80.0, 60.0)
1577        >>> tri.is_right()
1578        True
1579    """
1580
1581    def __init__(
1582        self,
1583        p1: PointType | Sequence[PointType],
1584        p2: PointType | None = None,
1585        p3: PointType | None = None,
1586        **kwargs: object,
1587    ) -> None:
1588        """Create a closed triangle.
1589
1590        Args:
1591            p1: First vertex, or a sequence of three vertices.
1592            p2: Second vertex when ``p1`` is a single point.
1593            p3: Third vertex when ``p1`` is a single point.
1594            **kwargs: Passed to ``Shape``.
1595
1596        Examples:
1597            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1598            >>> sg.Triangle((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60)).vertices
1599            ((0.0, 0.0), (60.0, 0.0), (0.0, 60.0))
1600            >>> sg.Triangle([(0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60)]).vertices
1601            ((0.0, 0.0), (60.0, 0.0), (0.0, 60.0))
1602        """
1603        if p2 is None and p3 is None:
1604            points = list(p1)
1605        elif p2 is None or p3 is None:
1606            raise ValueError("Triangle requires three vertices.")
1607        else:
1608            if not (
1609                check_position(p1) and check_position(p2) and check_position(p3)
1610            ):
1611                raise ValueError("Triangle vertices must be points.")
1612            points = [p1, p2, p3]
1613        if len(points) != 3:
1614            raise ValueError("Triangle requires three vertices.")
1615        kwargs = dict(kwargs)
1616        kwargs.setdefault("closed", True)
1617        kwargs.setdefault("subtype", Types.TRIANGLE)
1618        super().__init__(points, **kwargs)
1619        self.subtype = Types.TRIANGLE
1620
1621    def __repr__(self) -> str:
1622        """Return a Triangle string from this triangle's vertices.
1623
1624        Examples:
1625            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1626            >>> repr(sg.Triangle((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60)))
1627            'Triangle(((0.0, 0.0), (60.0, 0.0), (0.0, 60.0)))'
1628            >>> str(sg.Triangle((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))).startswith("Shape")
1629            True
1630        """
1631        if len(self.primary_points) == 0:
1632            return "Triangle()"
1633        if len(self.primary_points) < 4:
1634            return f"Triangle({self.vertices})"
1635        return f"Triangle([{self.vertices[0]}, ..., {self.vertices[-1]}])"
1636
1637    @property
1638    def p1(self) -> PointType:
1639        """First vertex."""
1640        return self.vertices[0]
1641
1642    @property
1643    def p2(self) -> PointType:
1644        """Second vertex."""
1645        return self.vertices[1]
1646
1647    @property
1648    def p3(self) -> PointType:
1649        """Third vertex."""
1650        return self.vertices[2]
1651
1652    def _pts(self) -> tuple[PointType, PointType, PointType]:
1653        return _triangle_vertices(self)
1654
1655    def signed_area(self) -> float:
1656        """Return the signed area."""
1657        return triangle_signed_area(*self._pts())
1658
1659    def area(self) -> float:
1660        """Return the unsigned area."""
1661        return triangle_area(*self._pts())
1662
1663    def perimeter(self) -> float:
1664        """Return the perimeter."""
1665        return triangle_perimeter(*self._pts())
1666
1667    def semiperimeter(self) -> float:
1668        """Return the semiperimeter."""
1669        return triangle_semiperimeter(*self._pts())
1670
1671    def side_lengths(self) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
1672        """Return side lengths opposite ``p1``, ``p2``, and ``p3``."""
1673        return triangle_side_lengths(*self._pts())
1674
1675    def longest_edge(self) -> tuple[PointType, PointType]:
1676        """Return the longest edge as a pair of vertices.
1677
1678        Examples:
1679            >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1680            >>> sg.Triangle((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 80)).longest_edge()
1681            ((60.0, 0.0), (0.0, 80.0))
1682        """
1683        return triangle_longest_edge(*self._pts())
1684
1685    def shortest_edge(self) -> tuple[PointType, PointType]:
1686        """Return the shortest edge as a pair of vertices.
1687
1688        Examples:

def triangle_opposite_edge( p1: Sequence[float], p2: Sequence[float], p3: Sequence[float], vertex_index: Sequence[float] | int) -> tuple[Sequence[float], Sequence[float]]: 
253def triangle_opposite_edge(
254    p1: PointType,
255    p2: PointType,
256    p3: PointType,
257    vertex_index: PointType | int,
258) -> tuple[PointType, PointType]:
259    """Return the edge opposite a vertex or vertex index.
260
261    Index ``0`` is ``p1`` (opposite ``(p2, p3)``), ``1`` is ``p2``
262    (opposite ``(p3, p1)``), and ``2`` is ``p3`` (opposite ``(p1, p2)``).
263
264    Examples:
265        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
266        >>> sg.triangle_opposite_edge((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 80), 0)
267        ((60.0, 0.0), (0.0, 80.0))
268        >>> sg.triangle_opposite_edge((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 80), (60, 0))
269        ((0.0, 80.0), (0.0, 0.0))
270    """
271    p1, p2, p3 = _xy(p1), _xy(p2), _xy(p3)
272    if vertex_index in (0, p1) or (
273        not isinstance(vertex_index, int) and equal_points(vertex_index, p1)
274    ):
275        return (p2, p3)
276    if vertex_index in (1, p2) or (
277        not isinstance(vertex_index, int) and equal_points(vertex_index, p2)
278    ):
279        return (p3, p1)
280    if vertex_index in (2, p3) or (
281        not isinstance(vertex_index, int) and equal_points(vertex_index, p3)
282    ):
283        return (p1, p2)
284    if isinstance(vertex_index, int):
285        raise ValueError("vertex index must be 0, 1, or 2.")
286    raise ValueError("vertex is not a vertex of this triangle.")

Return the edge opposite a vertex or vertex index.

Index 0 is p1 (opposite (p2, p3)), 1 is p2 (opposite (p3, p1)), and 2 is p3 (opposite (p1, p2)).

Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> sg.triangle_opposite_edge((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 80), 0)
((60.0, 0.0), (0.0, 80.0))
>>> sg.triangle_opposite_edge((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 80), (60, 0))
((0.0, 80.0), (0.0, 0.0))

def triangle_altitudes( p1: Sequence[float], p2: Sequence[float], p3: Sequence[float]) -> tuple[float, float, float]: 
314def triangle_altitudes(
315    p1: PointType, p2: PointType, p3: PointType
316) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
317    """Return altitude lengths to the sides opposite ``p1``, ``p2``, ``p3``.
318
319    Examples:
320        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
321        >>> sg.triangle_altitudes((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 80))
322        (48.0, 60.0, 80.0)
323    """
324    area = triangle_area(p1, p2, p3)
325    side_a, side_b, side_c = _side_lengths(p1, p2, p3)
326    if side_a == 0.0 or side_b == 0.0 or side_c == 0.0:
327        raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
328    return (2.0 * area / side_a, 2.0 * area / side_b, 2.0 * area / side_c)

Return altitude lengths to the sides opposite p1, p2, p3.

def triangle_medians( p1: Sequence[float], p2: Sequence[float], p3: Sequence[float]) -> tuple[float, float, float]: 
331def triangle_medians(
332    p1: PointType, p2: PointType, p3: PointType
333) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
334    """Return median lengths from ``p1``, ``p2``, and ``p3``.
335
336    Examples:
337        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
338        >>> medians = sg.triangle_medians((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
339        >>> tuple(round(length, 10) for length in medians)
340        (42.4264068712, 67.082039325, 67.082039325)
341    """
342    side_a, side_b, side_c = _side_lengths(p1, p2, p3)
343
344    def median_length(opp: float, adj_b: float, adj_c: float) -> float:
345        return 0.5 * sqrt(2.0 * adj_b * adj_b + 2.0 * adj_c * adj_c - opp * opp)
346
347    return (
348        median_length(side_a, side_b, side_c),
349        median_length(side_b, side_a, side_c),
350        median_length(side_c, side_a, side_b),
351    )

def triangle_2sides_angle( side1: float, angle: float, side2: float) -> Triangle: 
419def triangle_2sides_angle(side1: float, angle: float, side2: float) -> Triangle:
420    """Return a triangle from two sides and the included angle (SAS).
421
422    The included-angle vertex is at the origin. ``side1`` lies along the
423    positive x-axis. ``side2`` is placed at ``angle`` from that axis, so a
424    positive ``angle`` yields a counterclockwise triangle.
425
426    Args:
427        side1: Length of the side from the origin along the positive x-axis.
428        angle: Included angle at the origin, in radians.
429        side2: Length of the side from the origin at ``angle``.
430
431    Returns:
432        Triangle: Vertices at the origin, along the x-axis, and at ``angle``.
433
434    Examples:
435        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
436        >>> tri = sg.triangle_2sides_angle(60, sg.pi / 2, 80)
437        >>> tri.vertices
438        ((0.0, 0.0), (60.0, 0.0), (0.0, 80.0))
439        >>> tri.side_lengths()
440        (100.0, 80.0, 60.0)
441    """
442    if side1 <= 0.0 or side2 <= 0.0:
443        raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
444    if not (0.0 < angle < pi):
445        raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
446    _, abs_tol = resolve_tol()
447    p1 = (0.0, 0.0)
448    p2 = (float(side1) + 0.0, 0.0)
449    p3_x = side2 * cos(angle) + 0.0
450    p3_y = side2 * sin(angle) + 0.0
451    if abs(p3_x) <= abs_tol:
452        p3_x = 0.0
453    if abs(p3_y) <= abs_tol:
454        p3_y = 0.0
455    p3 = (p3_x, p3_y)
456    _require_positive_area(p1, p2, p3, abs_tol)
457    return Triangle(p1, p2, p3)

Return a triangle from two sides and the included angle (SAS).

The included-angle vertex is at the origin. side1 lies along the positive x-axis. side2 is placed at angle from that axis, so a positive angle yields a counterclockwise triangle.

Arguments:
  • side1: Length of the side from the origin along the positive x-axis.
  • angle: Included angle at the origin, in radians.
  • side2: Length of the side from the origin at angle.
Returns:

Triangle: Vertices at the origin, along the x-axis, and at angle.

Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> tri = sg.triangle_2sides_angle(60, sg.pi / 2, 80)
>>> tri.vertices
((0.0, 0.0), (60.0, 0.0), (0.0, 80.0))
>>> tri.side_lengths()
(100.0, 80.0, 60.0)
def triangle_2angles_side( angle_a: float, angle_b: float, side_a: float) -> Triangle: 
460def triangle_2angles_side(
461    angle_a: float, angle_b: float, side_a: float
462) -> Triangle:
463    """Return a triangle from two angles and the included side (ASA).
464
465    The vertex of ``angle_a`` is at the origin. The included side (between
466    that vertex and the vertex of ``angle_b``) lies along the positive
467    x-axis and has length ``side_a``. A positive construction yields a
468    counterclockwise triangle.
469
470    Args:
471        angle_a: Interior angle at the origin, in radians.
472        angle_b: Interior angle at the positive-x vertex, in radians.
473        side_a: Length of the included side, along the positive x-axis.
474
475    Returns:
476        Triangle: Vertices at the origin, along the x-axis, and at ``angle_a``.
477
478    Examples:
479        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
480        >>> tri = sg.triangle_2angles_side(sg.pi / 2, sg.pi / 4, 60)
481        >>> tri.vertices
482        ((0.0, 0.0), (60.0, 0.0), (0.0, 60.0))
483        >>> tuple(round(angle, 10) for angle in tri.angles())
484        (1.5707963268, 0.7853981634, 0.7853981634)
485    """
486    if side_a <= 0.0:
487        raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
488    if not (0.0 < angle_a < pi) or not (0.0 < angle_b < pi):
489        raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
490    angle_c = pi - angle_a - angle_b
491    if not (0.0 < angle_c < pi):
492        raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
493    side_b = law_of_sines_side(side_a, angle_c, angle_b)
494    return triangle_2sides_angle(side_a, angle_a, side_b)

Return a triangle from two angles and the included side (ASA).

The vertex of angle_a is at the origin. The included side (between that vertex and the vertex of angle_b) lies along the positive x-axis and has length side_a. A positive construction yields a counterclockwise triangle.

Arguments:
  • angle_a: Interior angle at the origin, in radians.
  • angle_b: Interior angle at the positive-x vertex, in radians.
  • side_a: Length of the included side, along the positive x-axis.
Returns:

Triangle: Vertices at the origin, along the x-axis, and at angle_a.

Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> tri = sg.triangle_2angles_side(sg.pi / 2, sg.pi / 4, 60)
>>> tri.vertices
((0.0, 0.0), (60.0, 0.0), (0.0, 60.0))
>>> tuple(round(angle, 10) for angle in tri.angles())
(1.5707963268, 0.7853981634, 0.7853981634)
def law_of_cosines_side(side_b: float, side_c: float, angle_a: float) -> float: 
497def law_of_cosines_side(side_b: float, side_c: float, angle_a: float) -> float:
498    """Return the side opposite ``angle_a`` from two sides and the included angle.
499
500    Examples:
501        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
502        >>> sg.law_of_cosines_side(60, 80, sg.pi / 2)
503        100.0
504    """
505    return sqrt(
506        side_b * side_b + side_c * side_c - 2.0 * side_b * side_c * cos(angle_a)
507    )

Return the side opposite angle_a from two sides and the included angle.

def law_of_cosines_angle(side_a: float, side_b: float, side_c: float) -> float: 
510def law_of_cosines_angle(side_a: float, side_b: float, side_c: float) -> float:
511    """Return the angle opposite ``side_a`` from three side lengths.
512
513    Examples:
514        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
515        >>> sg.law_of_cosines_angle(100, 80, 60) == sg.pi / 2
516        True
517    """
518    denom = 2.0 * side_b * side_c
519    if denom == 0.0:
520        raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
521    cosine = (side_b * side_b + side_c * side_c - side_a * side_a) / denom
522    cosine = max(-1.0, min(1.0, cosine))
523    return acos(cosine)

Return the angle opposite side_a from three side lengths.

Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> sg.law_of_cosines_angle(100, 80, 60) == sg.pi / 2
True
def law_of_sines_side(side_a: float, angle_a: float, angle_b: float) -> float: 
526def law_of_sines_side(side_a: float, angle_a: float, angle_b: float) -> float:
527    """Return the side opposite ``angle_b`` from one side and two angles.
528
529    Examples:
530        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
531        >>> round(sg.law_of_sines_side(60, sg.pi / 2, sg.pi / 6), 10)
532        30.0
533    """
534    if isclose(sin(angle_a), 0.0, rel_tol=0.0, abs_tol=1e-15):
535        raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
536    return side_a * sin(angle_b) / sin(angle_a)

666def is_right_triangle(
667    p1: PointType,
668    p2: PointType,

671    abs_tol: float | None = None,
672) -> bool:
673    """Return True if one angle is a right angle within tolerance.

def is_acute_triangle( p1: Sequence[float], p2: Sequence[float], p3: Sequence[float], rel_tol: float | None = None, abs_tol: float | None = None) -> bool: 
692def is_acute_triangle(
693    p1: PointType,
694    p2: PointType,
695    p3: PointType,
696    rel_tol: float | None = None,
697    abs_tol: float | None = None,
698) -> bool:
699    """Return True if all angles are acute.
700
701    Examples:
702        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
703        >>> sg.is_acute_triangle((0, 0), (60, 0), (30, 60))
704        True
705        >>> sg.is_acute_triangle((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 80))
706        False
707    """
708    rel_tol, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
709    if is_degenerate_triangle(p1, p2, p3, rel_tol, abs_tol):
710        return False
711    sides = sorted(_side_lengths(p1, p2, p3))
712    return (
713        sides[0] * sides[0] + sides[1] * sides[1]
714        > sides[2] * sides[2] + abs_tol
715    )

738    return (
739        sides[0] * sides[0] + sides[1] * sides[1]
740        < sides[2] * sides[2] - abs_tol
741    )

>>> sg.is_obtuse_triangle((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 80))
False
def triangle_orientation( p1: Sequence[float], p2: Sequence[float], p3: Sequence[float], rel_tol: float | None = None, abs_tol: float | None = None) -> int: 
744def triangle_orientation(
745    p1: PointType,
746    p2: PointType,
747    p3: PointType,
748    rel_tol: float | None = None,
749    abs_tol: float | None = None,
750) -> int:
751    """Return ``1`` if CCW, ``-1`` if CW, ``0`` if collinear.
752
753    Examples:
754        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
755        >>> sg.triangle_orientation((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
756        1
757        >>> sg.triangle_orientation((0, 0), (0, 60), (60, 0))
758        -1
759        >>> sg.triangle_orientation((0, 0), (40, 0), (80, 0))
760        0
761    """
762    _, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
763    signed = triangle_signed_area(p1, p2, p3)
764    if abs(signed) <= abs_tol:
765        return 0
766    if signed > 0:
767        return 1
768    return -1

def triangle_incenter( p1: Sequence[float], p2: Sequence[float], p3: Sequence[float]) -> Sequence[float]: 
829def triangle_incenter(p1: PointType, p2: PointType, p3: PointType) -> PointType:
830    """Return the incenter of triangle ``p1 p2 p3``.
831
832    Examples:
833        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
834        >>> sg.triangle_incenter((0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 60))
835        (20.0, 20.0)
836    """
837    side_a, side_b, side_c = _side_lengths(p1, p2, p3)
838    perimeter = side_a + side_b + side_c
839    if perimeter == 0.0:
840        raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
841    x1, y1 = p1[:2]
842    x2, y2 = p2[:2]
843    x3, y3 = p3[:2]
844    center_x = (side_a * x1 + side_b * x2 + side_c * x3) / perimeter
845    center_y = (side_a * y1 + side_b * y2 + side_c * y3) / perimeter
846    return (center_x, center_y)

Return the incenter of triangle p1 p2 p3.

Examples:

>>> sg.triangle_incenter((0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 60))
(20.0, 20.0)
def triangle_circumcenter( p1: Sequence[float], p2: Sequence[float], p3: Sequence[float]) -> Sequence[float]: 
849def triangle_circumcenter(
850    p1: PointType, p2: PointType, p3: PointType
851) -> PointType:
852    """Return the circumcenter of triangle ``p1 p2 p3``.
853
854    Examples:
855        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
856        >>> sg.triangle_circumcenter((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
857        (30.0, 30.0)
858    """
859    bisector_ab = perp_bisector((p1, p2))
860    bisector_ac = perp_bisector((p1, p3))
861    center = intersect(bisector_ab, bisector_ac)
862    if center is None:
863        raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
864    return _xy(center)

def triangle_orthocenter( p1: Sequence[float], p2: Sequence[float], p3: Sequence[float]) -> Sequence[float]: 
867def triangle_orthocenter(
868    p1: PointType, p2: PointType, p3: PointType
869) -> PointType:
870    """Return the orthocenter of triangle ``p1 p2 p3``.
871
872    Examples:
873        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
874        >>> sg.triangle_orthocenter((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
875        (0.0, 0.0)
876    """
877    centroid_x, centroid_y = triangle_centroid(p1, p2, p3)
878    circum_x, circum_y = triangle_circumcenter(p1, p2, p3)

880        3.0 * centroid_x - 2.0 * circum_x,
881        3.0 * centroid_y - 2.0 * circum_y,
882    )

def triangle_excenters( p1: Sequence[float], p2: Sequence[float], p3: Sequence[float]) -> tuple[Sequence[float], Sequence[float], Sequence[float]]: 
900def triangle_excenters(
901    p1: PointType, p2: PointType, p3: PointType
902) -> tuple[PointType, PointType, PointType]:
903    """Return the three excenters opposite ``p1``, ``p2``, and ``p3``.
904
905    Examples:
906        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
907        >>> centers = sg.triangle_excenters((0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 60))
908        >>> tuple(tuple(round(coord, 10) for coord in center) for center in centers)
909        ((120.0, 120.0), (-40.0, 40.0), (60.0, -60.0))
910    """
911    side_a, side_b, side_c = _side_lengths(p1, p2, p3)
912    x1, y1 = p1[:2]
913    x2, y2 = p2[:2]
914    x3, y3 = p3[:2]
915
916    def excenter(
917        opp: float,
918        adj_b: float,
919        adj_c: float,
920        px: float,
921        py: float,
922        qx: float,
923        qy: float,
924        rx: float,
925        ry: float,
926    ) -> PointType:
927        denom = -opp + adj_b + adj_c
928        if denom == 0.0:
929            raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
930        center_x = (-opp * px + adj_b * qx + adj_c * rx) / denom
931        center_y = (-opp * py + adj_b * qy + adj_c * ry) / denom
932        return (center_x, center_y)
933
934    return (
935        excenter(side_a, side_b, side_c, x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3),
936        excenter(side_b, side_a, side_c, x2, y2, x1, y1, x3, y3),
937        excenter(side_c, side_a, side_b, x3, y3, x1, y1, x2, y2),
938    )

Return the three excenters opposite p1, p2, and p3.

Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> centers = sg.triangle_excenters((0, 0), (80, 0), (0, 60))
>>> tuple(tuple(round(coord, 10) for coord in center) for center in centers)
((120.0, 120.0), (-40.0, 40.0), (60.0, -60.0))

def barycentric_coordinates( point: Sequence[float], triangle: Triangle | Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> tuple[float, float, float]: 
1016def barycentric_coordinates(
1017    point: PointType, triangle: TriangleLike
1018) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
1019    """Return barycentric weights of ``point`` with respect to ``triangle``.
1020
1021    Examples:
1022        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1023        >>> sg.barycentric_coordinates((0, 0), ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60)))
1024        (1.0, 0.0, 0.0)
1025        >>> sg.barycentric_coordinates((30, 30), ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60)))
1026        (0.0, 0.5, 0.5)
1027    """
1028    p1, p2, p3 = _triangle_vertices(triangle)
1029    area = triangle_signed_area(p1, p2, p3)
1030    if area == 0.0:
1031        raise ValueError("Degenerate triangle.")
1032    weight1 = triangle_signed_area(point, p2, p3) / area
1033    weight2 = triangle_signed_area(p1, point, p3) / area
1034    weight3 = triangle_signed_area(p1, p2, point) / area
1035    return (weight1, weight2, weight3)

Return barycentric weights of point with respect to triangle.

>>> sg.barycentric_coordinates((30, 30), ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60)))

1076def normalize_barycentric(
1077    weights: Sequence[float],

def triangle_contains_point_inclusive( triangle: Triangle | Sequence[Sequence[float]], point: Sequence[float], rel_tol: float | None = None, abs_tol: float | None = None) -> bool: 
1125def triangle_contains_point_inclusive(
1126    triangle: TriangleLike,
1127    point: PointType,
1128    rel_tol: float | None = None,
1129    abs_tol: float | None = None,
1130) -> bool:
1131    """Return True if ``point`` is inside ``triangle`` or on its boundary.
1132
1133    Examples:
1134        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1135        >>> tri = ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
1136        >>> sg.triangle_contains_point_inclusive(tri, (20, 20))
1137        True
1138        >>> sg.triangle_contains_point_inclusive(tri, (0, 0))
1139        True
1140        >>> sg.triangle_contains_point_inclusive(tri, (80, 80))
1141        False
1142    """
1143    rel_tol, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
1144    p1, p2, p3 = _triangle_vertices(triangle)
1145    if is_degenerate_triangle(p1, p2, p3, rel_tol, abs_tol):
1146        return False
1147    w1, w2, w3 = barycentric_coordinates(point, (p1, p2, p3))
1148    return (
1149        w1 >= -abs_tol
1150        and w2 >= -abs_tol
1151        and w3 >= -abs_tol
1152        and isclose(w1 + w2 + w3, 1.0, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol)
1153    )

Return True if point is inside triangle or on its boundary.

Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> tri = ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
>>> sg.triangle_contains_point_inclusive(tri, (20, 20))
True

def triangle_contains_point_strictly( triangle: Triangle | Sequence[Sequence[float]], point: Sequence[float], rel_tol: float | None = None, abs_tol: float | None = None) -> bool: 
1156def triangle_contains_point_strictly(
1157    triangle: TriangleLike,
1158    point: PointType,
1159    rel_tol: float | None = None,
1160    abs_tol: float | None = None,
1161) -> bool:
1162    """Return True if ``point`` is strictly inside ``triangle``.
1163
1164    Examples:
1165        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1166        >>> tri = ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))

1169        >>> sg.triangle_contains_point_strictly(tri, (0, 0))
1170        False
1171    """

1173    p1, p2, p3 = _triangle_vertices(triangle)
1174    if is_degenerate_triangle(p1, p2, p3, rel_tol, abs_tol):

def classify_point_in_triangle( triangle: Triangle | Sequence[Sequence[float]], point: Sequence[float], rel_tol: float | None = None, abs_tol: float | None = None) -> TrianglePointClass: 
1196def classify_point_in_triangle(
1197    triangle: TriangleLike,
1198    point: PointType,
1199    rel_tol: float | None = None,
1200    abs_tol: float | None = None,
1201) -> TrianglePointClass:
1202    """Classify ``point`` relative to ``triangle``.
1203
1204    Examples:
1205        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1206        >>> tri = ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
1207        >>> sg.classify_point_in_triangle(tri, (20, 20))
1208        <TrianglePointClass.INSIDE: 'Inside'>
1209        >>> sg.classify_point_in_triangle(tri, (0, 0))
1210        <TrianglePointClass.ON_VERTEX: 'OnVertex'>
1211        >>> sg.classify_point_in_triangle(tri, (30, 0))
1212        <TrianglePointClass.ON_EDGE: 'OnEdge'>
1213        >>> sg.classify_point_in_triangle(tri, (80, 80))
1214        <TrianglePointClass.OUTSIDE: 'Outside'>
1215    """
1216    rel_tol, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
1217    p1, p2, p3 = _triangle_vertices(triangle)
1218    if is_degenerate_triangle(p1, p2, p3, rel_tol, abs_tol):
1219        return TrianglePointClass.DEGENERATE
1220    if (
1221        equal_points(point, p1, rel_tol, abs_tol)
1222        or equal_points(point, p2, rel_tol, abs_tol)
1223        or equal_points(point, p3, rel_tol, abs_tol)
1224    ):
1225        return TrianglePointClass.ON_VERTEX
1226    if (
1227        on_segment(p1, p2, point, eps=abs_tol)
1228        or on_segment(p2, p3, point, eps=abs_tol)
1229        or on_segment(p3, p1, point, eps=abs_tol)
1230    ):
1231        return TrianglePointClass.ON_EDGE
1232    if triangle_contains_point_strictly(triangle, point, rel_tol, abs_tol):
1233        return TrianglePointClass.INSIDE
1234    return TrianglePointClass.OUTSIDE

Classify point relative to triangle.

Examples:

>>> tri = ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
>>> sg.classify_point_in_triangle(tri, (20, 20))
<TrianglePointClass.INSIDE: 'Inside'>
>>> sg.classify_point_in_triangle(tri, (0, 0))
<TrianglePointClass.ON_VERTEX: 'OnVertex'>
>>> sg.classify_point_in_triangle(tri, (30, 0))
<TrianglePointClass.ON_EDGE: 'OnEdge'>
>>> sg.classify_point_in_triangle(tri, (80, 80))
<TrianglePointClass.OUTSIDE: 'Outside'>

def intersect_segment_triangle( segment: Sequence[Sequence], triangle: Triangle | Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> TriangleIntersection: 
1315def intersect_segment_triangle(
1316    segment: LineType, triangle: TriangleLike
1317) -> TriangleIntersection:
1318    """Intersect a line segment with ``triangle``.
1319
1320    Examples:
1321        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1322        >>> hit = sg.intersect_segment_triangle(
1323        ...     [(-60, 15), (60, 15)], ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
1324        ... )
1325        >>> hit.kind
1326        <TriangleIntersectionKind.SEGMENT: 'A segment'>
1327        >>> hit.points
1328        ((45.0, 15.0), (0.0, 15.0))
1329    """
1330    p1, p2, p3 = _triangle_vertices(triangle)
1331    start, end = _xy(segment[0]), _xy(segment[1])
1332    points: list[PointType] = []
1333    if triangle_contains_point_inclusive((p1, p2, p3), start):
1334        points.append(start)
1335    if triangle_contains_point_inclusive((p1, p2, p3), end):
1336        points.append(end)
1337    for edge in ((p1, p2), (p2, p3), (p3, p1)):
1338        kind, hit = intersection((start, end), edge)
1339        if kind == Connection.INTERSECT and hit is not None:
1340            points.append(_xy(hit))
1341    return _intersection_from_points(points)

def intersect_ray_triangle( ray: Sequence[Sequence], triangle: Triangle | Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> RayTriangleHit | None: 
1344def intersect_ray_triangle(
1345    ray: LineType, triangle: TriangleLike
1346) -> RayTriangleHit | None:
1347    """Intersect a ray with ``triangle``.
1348
1349    ``ray`` is ``(origin, point_on_ray)``. The first hit along the ray is
1350    returned, or ``None`` if the ray misses.
1351
1352    Examples:
1353        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1354        >>> hit = sg.intersect_ray_triangle(
1355        ...     [(-60, 15), (60, 15)], ((0, 0), (60, 0), (0, 60))
1356        ... )
1357        >>> hit.point
1358        (0.0, 15.0)
1359        >>> hit.distance
1360        60.0
1361        >>> hit.front_facing
1362        True
1363    """
1364    origin = _xy(ray[0])
1365    through = _xy(ray[1])
1366    direction = (through[0] - origin[0], through[1] - origin[1])
1367    p1, p2, p3 = _triangle_vertices(triangle)
1368    _, abs_tol = resolve_tol()
1369    candidates: list[PointType] = []
1370    if triangle_contains_point_inclusive((p1, p2, p3), origin):
1371        candidates.append(origin)
1372    for point in _edge_hits_with_line((origin, through), (p1, p2, p3)):
1373        param = _ray_param(origin, direction, point)
1374        if param >= -abs_tol:
1375            candidates.append(point)
1376    unique = _unique_points(candidates)
1377    if not unique:
1378        return None
1379    hit_point = min(
1380        unique, key=lambda point: _ray_param(origin, direction, point)
1381    )
1382    return RayTriangleHit(
1383        point=hit_point,
1384        distance=distance(origin, hit_point),
1385        barycentric_coordinates=barycentric_coordinates(
1386            hit_point, (p1, p2, p3)
1387        ),
1388        front_facing=is_counterclockwise(p1, p2, p3),
1389    )

>>> hit.distance
